steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place decorating sugar in a small bowl (or use several colors and separate bowls).

Beat shortening and butter in the bowl of a stand mixer until smooth and creamy, 2 to 3 minutes. Mix in sugar until incorporated, then mix in eggs, one at a time, scraping the sides of the bowl as necessary. Mix in vanilla.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl until combined. Gradually add to the wet ingredients and mix until incorporated and the dough comes together.
Roll dough into walnut-sized balls. Roll each ball in sugar to coat, then place 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until light brown on the bottoms, 10 to 12 minutes, switching racks halfway through. Remove from the oven and transfer to wire racks to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Soft Sugar Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This soft sugar cookie recipe is quick and easy to make. Use any color sugar to make these for holidays, birthdays, or other special occasions.

review.reviewBody: We used this recipe for rolled out cookies. I baked them for 11 minute- I took them out before they started to brown,as we wanted super soft cookies. They came out great. The dough held its shape well, and didnt require chilling before rolling and cutting. I found it very easy to work with. I sprinkled one pan with cinnamon and sugar before baking- they were great! The kids used frosting on some of them. Since they are not super sweet on their own, the frosting isnt to much. edit to add: we've made this recipe a few times now. Its even better if you add the zest of one medium orange. It gives them a bit more flavor.

Absolutely wonderful! Be sure to cream the butter, shortening, and sugar together until mixture is light and fluffy before proceding to next step. This will make a big difference. Also, it helps to chill the dough before rolling into balls. This is the best sugar cookie I've ever tasted! It's a keeper!

Dont you hate it when someone gives a review of less than 5 stars and then goes on to say they didnt have all the ingredients so they substituted butter for shortening?... I found these cookies to be great. They baked up nice and soft. I will keep this recipe and use it from now on.

Disregard negative reviews; when you follow the recipe by using the given ingredients without making any substitutions (with the exception of the salt which I reduced to 1/2 teaspoon), the cookies turn out perfect. The only change that I made was reducing the kosher salt down from 1 teaspoon to 1/2 teaspoon. Be mindful that fine sea salt is saltier than kosher salt so if a recipe calls for 1 teaspoon of kosher salt, you only need 1/2 teaspoon of sea salt. The amount of sugar was perfect. I enjoyed making them with my nieces and nephew. The cookie dough was easy to shape by hand, creating a sensory and fun experience for the kids. I creamed the butter, shortening, and sugar by hand, added vanilla, eggs, salt, and the remaining dry ingredients. Chilling the dough for 20 mins made shaping easy. After rolling into balls, we squished them into 1/2-inch-thick circles and dipped them in sprinkles and baked them for 10 mins at 350°F.

Ok so I’m not a baker by any means but because of Covid I’m not able to do my usual volunteer work. So I signed up to bake cookies to send to our soldiers abroad. This recipe makes me look I’ve been baking for years. The only thing I had to change was swapping all butter for shortening as recommended by the organization to keep the cookie from going rancid before reaching destination. I used butter flavor crisco and added 4 tsp of water to account for the conversion. The batter was ridiculously easy to work with after mixing so I decided not to refrigerate as I originally planned. I dipped in Halloween colored sprinkles and baked. The cookies turned out awesome! Buttery and chewy with the right amount of sweetness! We almost ate them all and I had to make a second batch so I would have enough to ship!! This recipe is great and I’ll be using this as my “go to” cookie batter for sure! Thanks for sharing!!!!

I've finally found a 'go-to' sugar cookie recipe. I love the crisp exterior on a soft cookie. I added a bit of orange extract to the dough. I weighed my balls before dipping in the sugar and flattening to 1/4 with the bottom of a glass. This gave me a uniform size. These cookies are wonderful as is, or frosted and decorated.

Fantastic! I used very little salt, maybe a half teaspoon at most since I used salted butter. I rolled the dough balls (snicker doodles style) in raw sugar to give it a pleasant crunch shell to the super soft innards. I did add in colored sugar with the raw to give it a festive Christmas look this time around.

I wanted to make the cookies harder, so I extended the baking time on a baking stone from 12 to about 18 minutes, and the sugar cookies really firmed up nicely. Since the cookies don't flatten out too much as others had mentioned, I simply used my fingers to flatten the dough. The sugar helps keep the cookies from sticking.

I used 2/3 cup cold butter and 2/3 cup shortening, reduced temperature to 325 degrees and pulled cookies out after 14 minutes. Soft inside and once cooled on a pre chilled cookie sheet firm on edges. I added a teaspoon of almond extract with the vanilla extract for perfect taste.

I love these cookies. They come together fast and are soft. I made they exactly as written the first time. I understand what people were saying about the salt. I liked it, but my family did not. The second time I made them I mixed the salt in with the eggs before blending the eggs into the batter. The cookies were just as good but without the salty taste. Solved!

I made these a couple of months ago on Valentine’s Day for my boyfriend. Delicious! The only substitution I made to the later batches was to turn the heat up about 5-10 degrees and cut the baking time down to like 8 or so minutes before letting them cool and set for at least twenty more minutes. The result is a soft chewy cookie. Thanks for this recipe!
These were so soft and delicious. I did refrigerate the dough for about an hour. I made them for Easter and rolled them in pastel colored sugars. I’ll be making these again!
It was go to at bake sale and a group order client and customers loved it

My sugar cookies came out delicious! I added a dash of cinnamon to the dough and sugar coating, and I folded in Christmas sprinkles (then pressed into cookie prior to baking). I love my cookies thicker so I will be keeping this recipe!
I didn't make any changes, recipe was really easy to follow. will make again . 😃 husband love them
They were soft and tasted like sugar cookies should. I rolled them in cinnamon and sugar and my family ate them all up! I'll definitely use this recipe going forward.
I needed a quick recipe to make for work. This recipe is very quick to put together and got rave reviews at work. I only had orange colored sugar but I plan to get more colors to make more.
The flavor is amazing but i think i accidently added to much flour because the cookies didn't really have a cookie shape more like a upside down bowl shape but overall i definitely recommend this!

I have a gentleman friend that craves soft cookies! I wanted to treat him after a stressful day. I found these and the reviews raved...and they have never let me down! These are awesome! Soft, but not heavy in any way. I also used real butter with the butter flavored shortening. The sweet and buttery flavor was amazing. If food is the way to a mans heart...these cookies will keep him around a long time. The recipe I have used from my mother for the past 20 years hit the shredder. Sorry Mom :) Follow-up guilty admission! I was having one of those days that nothing seems to go right. I wanted to splurge on my favorite "make me feel good treats", so I combined them! I made this recipe, (turned out great again)and let cool. In the mean time, I coarsely chopped Pecans and melted a bag of caramels. I dipped the tops of the cooled cookies into the caramel, pressed them into the chopped pecans, and when the caramel was cool, melted a bag of chocolate chips and once the melted chocolate started to cool, spread it all over the top of the cookies. Probably not the first one to think of it...but after a couple, all was well in the world of gayle again! **For those who said they don't spread. After you roll the balls in sugar, place them on the baking pan. Grab a small glass and lightly press the cookies into a disk. Don't squash them, but it will help.

Was looking for a classic sugar cookie recipe and this one more than delivers! The dough came together beautifully...very easy to work with, and I loved both the taste and the simplicity of decorating with colored sugar. I made these for a Fat Tuesday gathering and decorated them accordingly. Followed the recipe with the only modifications being: flattened the cookies slightly before baking and only dipped the top in the decorating sugar. Love love love these!!
